statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5324?
statutory.answer: No. On these facts, 31 U.S.C. § 5324 does not clearly apply because there is no cash deposit/withdrawal or other transaction structured around the $10,000 CTR threshold, nor evidence of intent to evade reporting; § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade reporting.
statutory.label: contradiction
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits (among other things) structuring or attempting to structure a transaction with a domestic financial institution for the purpose of evading the reporting requirements of 31 U.S.C. § 5313(a) (CTR reporting generally triggered by currency transactions over $10,000), and also prohibits causing or attempting to cause a financial institution to fail to file a required report. Here, the listed cash activity consists of multiple ATM cash withdrawals in the ~$290–$774 range, none near or above $10,000 and no pattern of breaking up a single large currency transaction into sub-$10,000 parts; the two wires ($3,726.74 and $7,602.20) are not “currency transactions” for CTR purposes and are not shown to be structured to evade a specific reporting requirement. The fact pattern also provides no evidence of the required mens rea—i.e., that the individual acted “for the purpose of evading” a reporting requirement or caused/attempted to cause non-filing. Therefore the elements of § 5324 (a structured transaction + purpose to evade a required report) are not satisfied on these facts; § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade reporting.
